evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna never says 'this will take 10–15 minutes' or asks for explicit buy-in before probing. She jumps straight to 'just to confirm that the apartment where we're coming from...'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Not asked. Joanna opens with 'Do you have any important concerns or instructions for this move' (customer says no), then moves directly into logistics probing without asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer raised no concerns in Section 2.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — customer raised no concerns to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Covered: property type (apartment), rooms (2 bedroom), furniture (bedroom sets, couches, kitchen table, nightstand/TV stand, bookshelves), boxes (10 estimated), parking (driveway and street, 30–40 feet walk). Missed: floor/stories (first floor mentioned late), special considerations (dog crates mentioned in context but not a formal probe), additional stops (not asked).
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes: 'how about four boxes typically we end up with the 25 to 35 boxes. Do you think you would just fall within that range?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Anchored: 'typically, a two bedroom apartment usually takes three and a half to five and a half hours to complete... I'll just put it more on the four to five hour mark, which is an estimated budget of $1,040.' Personalized to customer's plan to move smaller items: 'if you're planning to move the smaller items yourself that's totally fine, of course, the shorter to move the lower the cost.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Trip fee / overnight fee / packing materials: 'everything is already in that price. No other fees outside of it.' Minimum and increment framing: 'we just have a two and a half hour minimum. Once we go over, we only charge on every fifteen minute interval.' Damage coverage ('no worries coverage') and assembly/reassembly included in price stated.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Joanna gives the estimate and then says 'So you only pay for how long it takes after the two and a half hour minimum isn't it okay' — no 'Does that feel fair?' question and no pause held.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Partial. Mentioned ('on time guarantee. If we run time we schedule we provide this for you move') but no detail on discount terms or when it starts discounting.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Partial. Mentioned ('we will include our no worries, damage coverage which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any accidental damages') but lacks the no-deductible / no-fine-print framing.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Joanna lists the two promises but does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or any version of looping back to confirm they address the customer's concerns (which were never formally gathered anyway).
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Joanna says 'If you have any further questions or concerns, just let us know, okay?' — a throwaway 'any questions' framing, not 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No. Never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Joanna never says 'Would you like our help with your move?' She moves from pricing directly to 'may I please have your apartment number' and 'I'll send you your final confirmation email.' The booking is treated as a given, not a requested decision.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed: date (tomorrow), addresses (11900 Stone Hallow Drive → apartment 6112, first floor), arrival window (12:30–2:30 PM), price ($1,040 estimate). Missing: phone number (not asked), crew size (two movers mentioned in passing but not confirmed), notes for crew about customer's concerns (not left).

top_strength: Joanna gathered detailed furniture and logistics information early and personalized the estimate to the customer's stated plan to move smaller items herself, showing active listening in context.
coaching_note: Joanna must start every call with the quid pro quo framing (time-boxed, dependable quote promise) and explicit wait for buy-in before probing; she skipped this entirely and jumped straight into logistics, setting a passive tone that carried through to never asking for the business.
